biography.plain_text: Sietse Jelle Koopmans is a Dutch engineer and entrepreneur who developed and sold oilfield-equipment maker ASEP before founding energy-technology group Paradigm. He also founded and owns Zeelander Yachts, a family-run boutique Dutch shipyard known for quiet, sculpturally curved motor yachts. His work combines patented well-intervention engineering with international specialist shipbuilding.

long_biography.plain_text:
Five years of development culminated in Sietse Koopmans launching the Zeelander Z44 in 2008. Its rounded surfaces, quiet machinery and commuter-yacht proportions established a distinctive design language for the boutique shipyard he had created when the market offered no dayboat he wanted to own. The range later expanded while remaining deliberately low-volume and made to order.

Koopmans brought an engineer's precision to that experiment. Building from an industrial platform established with his father, he helped turn ASEP into a market-leading oilfield-equipment manufacturer and contributed patented well-intervention technology before the business was sold. Long-distance cruising then supplied a second education: years of practical observation shaped his insistence on comfort, silence and usability. The same product-led approach now spans Zeelander and his energy-technology interests.
